item.title: On the Laugesen--Siudeja Conjecture: A Sharp Lower Bound and Failure of the Upper Bound
item.description: arXiv:2611.27370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the sharp lower bound in the Laugesen--Siudeja conjecture and give a counterexample to its upper bound. For every bounded convex planar domain, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_1$, the area $A$, and the centroidal polar moment of inertia $I$ satisfy $\lambda_1A^3/I>9\pi^2/2$. The constant is approached by thin isosceles triangles. The lower bound follows from a rectangle comparison in the principal directions of the covariance matrix and a planar random-triangle inequality. For the upper bound, we exhibit an isosceles trapezoid on which $\lambda_1A^3/I>12\pi^2$, using Temple's inequality and exact arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Zhengchao Ji

item.title: A Higher-Dimensional Extension of the Laugesen--Siudeja Lower Bound
item.description: arXiv:2611.27678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a higher-dimensional analogue of the lower bound in the Laugesen--Siudeja conjecture, using a covariance normalization of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue. We give a covariance-dependent lower bound for every bounded convex domain. From this bound we obtain the optimal constant for convex planar domains and for simplices in every dimension \(d\geq2\). If the simplex covariance inequality stated in a 2026 preprint holds, the same constant is optimal over all bounded convex domains in dimensions \(d\geq3\). In each of these cases, the infimum is approached by compressing a regular simplex in the direction of an edge and is unattained.
item.dc:creator: Zhengchao Ji

item.title: A proof of the polygonal Faber--Krahn inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.27968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for every integer $n\ge3$, the regular $n$-gon uniquely minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, up to congruence, among simple polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides. We also obtain the optimal linear correction when fewer than $n$ sides are present. The proof combines a partition into convex cells with a mixed boundary comparison. Among convex polygons of fixed area and fixed sum of base angles less than $\pi$, the isosceles triangle minimizes the first eigenvalue with Dirichlet conditions on the base and Neumann conditions elsewhere. A comparison of Fourier transforms of conformal area densities proves this inequality and the corresponding upper bounds for inverse spectral moments of integer order at least two. We prove strict log-convexity of an interpolation of the eigenvalues of regular polygons of unit area for real parameters at least four. We then derive sharp hexagonal bounds for periodic convex polygonal tilings and asymptotic bounds for convex polygonal partitions of a fixed convex polygon, with an explicit correction for boundary junctions.
item.dc:creator: Yutian Li

item.title: Boundary remainders and optimal convergence rates for planar spectral partitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $S_m(\Omega)$ denote the infimum of the sum of the first Dirichlet eigenvalues over partitions of a bounded connected planar domain $\Omega$ into exactly $m$ nonempty connected open cells. We study the convergence of $|\Omega|S_m(\Omega)/m^2$ to its universal limit $c_*$. If the full topological boundary has zero area, we bound the absolute error by the area of its tubular neighborhood at scale $m^{-1/2}$, together with an $O(m^{-1/2})$ term. This yields rates $O_\Omega(m^{-1/2})$ on Lipschitz domains and $O_\Omega(m^{-\alpha/2})$ on domains with finitely many $C^{0,\alpha}$ boundary charts, $0<\alpha<1$, for all sufficiently large integers. The square and a fixed smooth domain have positive matching lower bounds of order $m^{-1/2}$. For each $\alpha\in(0,1)$, a fixed H\"older graph domain attains the order $m^{-\alpha/2}$ along a subsequence. Little H\"older domains satisfy the corresponding little-$o$ estimate, but no prescribed additional factor tending to zero works for the whole class, even with domain-dependent constants. An auxiliary energy with variable cell count gives the boundary estimate; a positive correction on the square and sparse graph constructions yield the lower bounds.
item.dc:creator: Yufan Cen

item.title: Eigenvalues and Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator in the Large-Friction Limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.26664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator by the methods of analytic dilation and phase-space deformation. We prove that in the large-friction limit $\gamma\to+\infty$, there are neither eigenvalues nor resonances away from the thresholds $\gamma N$, and that near each threshold $\gamma k$, there exists a bijection between the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and those of the Witten Laplacian at the level $k$, $-\Delta_V^{(k)}=-\Delta_V\otimes 1_{\mu_k}-d\Gamma_k(\operatorname{Hess}V)$. We also show that each negative eigenvalue of $-\Delta_V^{(k)}$, $k\geq 1$, produces a pole of the resolvent at distance of order $\gamma^{-1}$ below $\gamma k$, whose imaginary part is $O(e^{-c\gamma})$ for every $c<2\delta_V$. Here $\delta_V$ is the width of a strip of analyticity of $V$.
item.dc:creator: Xue Ping Wang (LMJL)

item.title: The regular $N$-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most $N$ sides and fixed area
item.description: arXiv:2611.26729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Phi(P)=|P|\mu_1(P)$, where $\mu_1(P)$ is the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of $P$. For every $N\ge3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes $\Phi$, up to congruence, among simple polygons of fixed area with at most $N$ sides. The values $\Phi(R_N)$ increase strictly with $N$. The maximization theorem answers Laugesen's question \cite[Problem~(1), p.~405]{ABLW} and proves the polygonal Szeg\H{o}--Weinberger conjecture of Laugesen and Siudeja \cite[Conjecture~6.36]{LSH}. It also implies that the triangular lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of the Voronoi cell at fixed covolume.
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo, Bingbing Xie

item.title: One exponential or two? Invertibility tests for Jordan epimorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.27850v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How many exponential factors must one test to recognise a Jordan epimorphism? Let \(T\colon A\to B\) be a unital linear surjection between complex Banach algebras, with \(B\) semisimple. Using a spectral-isometry theorem of Aznay and Chabbabi, we show that it suffices for \(T\) to send every product of two exponentials to an invertible element to force $T$ to be Jordan. If only single exponentials are tested, \(T\) is a Jordan epimorphism if and only if its kernel is a two-sided ideal, or equivalently a left ideal. A resolvent estimate on a logarithmic spiral shows that a single exponential suffices when the source is a \(C^*\)-algebra or the group algebra \(\ell^1(G)\) of a discrete group. A separate argument, which does not use the spectral-isometry theorem, shows that a single exponential also suffices when the target is a \(C^*\)-algebra with a faithful family of tracial states.
item.dc:creator: Catalin Badea

item.title: Exit-Pair Rigidity, Neutral Restart Laws, and Inverse Reconstruction in One Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.27853v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For an absorbed one-dimensional diffusion, we characterize two-point restart laws preserving the exit-side probability for every independent renewal clock. Spectral identities establish rigidity under spatial accumulation, while explicit nonsymmetric potentials admit neutral pairs. We distinguish midpoint Dirichlet isospectrality from Weyl reflection rigidity and prove a second-order high-energy asymptotic under local continuity, giving two necessary asymmetry conditions for neutral pairs. Two complete exit profiles at distinct reset rates identify diffusivity and drift; a finite birth-death analogue admits exact Jacobi criteria and reconstruction from four channel functions.
item.dc:creator: Tony Newton, Juan Antonio Vega Coso

item.title: Intervals of limit points for $B_{\alpha}$-spectral radii
item.description: arXiv:2611.27937v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let \[ B_{\alpha}(G)=\alpha A(G)+(1-\alpha)L(G)=(1-\alpha)D(G)+(2\alpha-1)A(G),\qquad 0\leq \alpha\leq 1. \] We study the limit points of the spectral radii of these matrices. Put $a_{\alpha}=1-\alpha$, $b_{\alpha}=|2\alpha-1|$, and $w_{\alpha}=a_{\alpha}+b_{\alpha}$. We prove that, for every $\alpha\neq 1/2$ and every integer $d\geq 3$, the interval \[ \left[a_{\alpha}d+2b_{\alpha}\sqrt{d-1},\,w_{\alpha}d\right] \] consists entirely of $B_{\alpha}$-limit points. All these points are realized by connected bipartite graphs of maximum degree at most $d$. We extend the induced-subgraph interpolation of Alon and Wei from $A$ to $aD+bA$, and obtain a unified proof using bipartite Ramanujan graphs. Consecutive intervals overlap for large $d$; hence the set of $B_{\alpha}$-limit points contains a half-line for every $\alpha\neq 1/2$. At $\alpha=1/2$, one has $B_{1/2}=D/2$, and the set of spectral radii is discrete. Combining uniform edge subdivisions with generalized Bethe decorations, we improve the Laplacian and signless Laplacian half-line to $[29/5,\infty)$, verified by an exact rational certificate. We also treat two complementary tree constructions. For the starlike trees $T_{1,m,m}$, the limiting $B_{\alpha}$-spectral radius is the unique solution above the path threshold of an explicit unsquared equation. More generally, letting selected arms of a starlike tree tend to infinity produces ordered limit points with tree realizations. Finally, we give the exact affine relations among $B_{\alpha}$, the $A_{\beta}$-matrix, and the deformed Laplacian. These identify which tree and caterpillar results are reparametrizations of earlier work. The interval theorem also yields half-lines of $A_\beta$-limit points for every $0\le\beta<1$, and of deformed-Laplacian limit points for every nonzero deformation parameter.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Belardo, Callum Huntington, Elismar R. Oliveira, Vilmar Trevisan

item.title: Optimal long-time derivative estimates for underdamped Langevin dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.25961v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the long-time behaviour of derivatives of the semigroup $P_t=e^{t\mathcal{A}}$ generated by the underdamped Langevin (kinetic Fokker-Planck) operator $\mathcal{A}$ on $L^2(\mu)$, where the Gibbs measure $\mu$ is not required to be finite. Under a weighted relative bound on the Hessian of the potential, we prove that for every integer $m\ge 0$ the squared $L^2(\mu)$ norms of $\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ and of $\nabla_{x,v}\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ are bounded by $C_m t^{-2m}\|h_0\|^2$ and $D_m t^{-(2m+1)}\|h_0\|^2$ respectively for large times, and the free dynamics shows that these exponents are optimal. The proof rests on a resolvent estimate near the imaginary axis, valid for every smooth potential, which follows from the adjoint relation between the generator and the velocity reversal and from the Gaussian Poincar\'e inequality in the velocity variable.
item.dc:creator: Lukang Sun

item.title: Small scale quantum ergodicity in cat maps
item.description: arXiv:2005.00648v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study small scale quantum ergodicity in quantum cat maps, with semiclassical parameter 1/N, and prove three groups of results. First, for every N and every eigenbasis, almost all eigenstates are equidistributed on phase space balls of radius (log N)^(-a) for a<1/2, and on position space balls for a<1. For a set of N of full density and for Hecke eigenbases, almost all eigenstates, and even all of them, are equidistributed at polynomial scales. Second, every invariant probability measure is the semiclassical measure of quasimodes of order 1/log N, one for each N, that are not equidistributed at any scale between 4N^(-1/8) and a prescribed scale tending to zero. Third, there are orthonormal bases of quasimodes of order 1/log N for every N, and eigenbases for N with short periods, in which a full density subset is equidistributed at every fixed scale, but not at the scales (log N)^(-a) for a>1/2 in phase space and a>1 in position space. Hence, the exponents 1/2 and 1 in the first group are sharp: even for a full density subset of eigenstates, quantum ergodicity at fixed scales does not extend beyond the critical logarithmic scales.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolong Han

item.title: A P\"oschl--Teller approximation to the wave equation outside a torus
item.description: arXiv:2505.15264v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a short-time parametrix for the exterior Dirichlet wave equation on the complement of a solid torus. The construction involves freezing one coefficient of the conjugated Laplacian. This results in a family of radial P\"oschl--Teller equations. We bound the $L^2$ error in terms of the energy of the initial data. We then give several examples of Gaussian wavepackets in toroidal coordinates.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Quirchmayr, Alden Waters

item.title: An indefinite Coulomb interaction from the Steklov spectrum of perforated manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.25211v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish optimal convergence rates for Steklov eigenvalues and harmonically extended eigenfunctions toward their weighted Laplace--Beltrami counterparts on a closed manifold perforated by many small geodesic balls. The holes have radii that scale critically with respect to their spacing in the sense that the boundary area of each hole balances with the weighted volume of its Voronoi cell. We then derive a higher-order expansion of the Steklov eigenvalues; in dimensions two and three, we identify two correction scales. The expansion is governed by an indefinite Coulomb-type energy of the discrepancy between the boundary and bulk measures, mediated by the reduced Green function of the limiting operator. The proof relies on sharp estimates for certain auxiliary functions that we introduce in order to quantify the discrepancy measure between the surface measure on the holes and their background density. Our paper serves to bridge an emerging literature in spectral geometry with one on systems of points interacting via Coulomb-type energies.
item.dc:creator: Zhonggan Huang, Raghavendra Venkatraman

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37423v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the sharp bound $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$ for the threefold additive energy of every lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, with an absolute constant. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ estimate for eigenfunctions on $\mathbb{T}^2$, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical uniform $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and confirms Bourgain's conjecture in this range. For all $k\ge4$, we obtain the fixed power saving for the $k$-fold additive energy $J_k(P_n)\le C|P_n|^{2k-3-\delta}$, with absolute constants $C,\delta>0$. Applications include mean-square convergence of observables and the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Absence of binding for the helium anion
item.description: arXiv:2611.19370v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the helium anion in the nonrelativistic Coulomb model with an infinitely massive nucleus and spin-$\frac12$ electrons. We prove the absence of binding, with $E^{\mathrm{F}}(3,2)=E^{\mathrm{F}}(2,2)$ and no three-electron ground state. A decomposition relative to the helium ground state and completion of the square reduce the problem to a one-dimensional variational inequality.
item.dc:creator: Hao Liang
